text.first-impression: Jeong, people meet you and feel like you're paying attention. Because you are. Ten seconds in, you've noticed their mood, their nervous hands, and that the person beside them is lying about something. You're warm but not loud, a candle rather than a bonfire. People feel safe telling you things. What they don't see: you're also deciding whether they're safe for you. And most of them don't pass. You're friendly with many and close to very few, and the few have no idea how hard the exam was. Maybe make the exam a little easier.
text.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you overthink. Professionally. One ambiguous text and you've written a three-act play, cast it, and cried at the ending. You also hold onto hurts, quietly, for years. You'll say it's fine and then remember the exact date it wasn't. And your mood can change the temperature of a room without you saying a single word. You don't need to stop feeling deeply. Please don't. You need to tell people what you feel before it hardens into a grudge they didn't know they were earning. Say it small and early. It's kinder.
text.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you're intense, devoted, and very attentive. Wonderful. Also occasionally a lot. Your sabotage move is reading signs instead of asking questions. They're quiet, you assume they're losing interest, you pull back first to protect yourself, and now they're confused about why you've gone cold. It's a self-fulfilling candle. Ask. Use your words. You're fantastic with words when you're not scared. And remember that not everyone who's calm is cold. Some people are just calm. It's a personality, not a verdict. Before you pull back, send one honest text instead. You'll be amazed how often it fixes everything.
text.friends-and-work: At work you're the one who notices what everyone else missed: the detail, the nuance, the vibe in the meeting. But you take criticism personally and replay it at 1am like a podcast nobody asked for. With friends you're the deep-talk friend, the one people call when it's real. You also keep score a little, quietly. Who replied, who forgot, who didn't ask. Your friends aren't always failing you. Sometimes they're just busy, tired, or bad at texting. Give them the benefit of the doubt you'd want. Also, delete the 1am podcast. Nobody's listening.
text.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm just being realistic. No. Sometimes you're being scared and calling it realism because it sounds wiser. You also tell yourself that if you show all your feelings, people will leave. Some might. The right ones won't. Hiding your feelings doesn't keep people close. It just means they end up loving a version of you with the volume turned right down, and you end up lonely in a room full of people who like you. Turn the volume up one notch this week. Just one. See who leans in instead of leaving.
text.the-fix: The fix, because Bom keeps tapping my shoulder. Give your overthinking a timer: twenty minutes, then do something with your hands. Say one hurt out loud within a day of it happening, not a year later in a fight about something else. Assume good intent once a day, as a little experiment, and see what happens. In love, ask the question instead of reading the sign. You have the most beautiful kind of light, the close, warm kind. Let people sit near it without testing them first. Most of them only want to get warm.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Jeong. You've reread that text nine times. It says 'ok'.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Perceptive, yes. Also writing a tragedy about a full stop.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You pull back first so nobody can leave you. Clever. Exhausting.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: True. So ask the question. Words. Out loud. Today.

spring.intro: Spring Jeong, Wood ran your birth season and feeds your candle, so you've got plenty of emotional fuel and you burn it on one subject at a time. Currently that's probably a person, a show or a grudge. People see someone soft, attentive and lovely. They don't see the archive. You remember everything: what they said, how they said it, and the date. Your red flag is keeping receipts in your heart and bringing them out months later. In love you're devoted and secretly keeping score. At work you're the quiet one who notices every slight. The fix: say it within forty-eight hours or let it go. No more vintage grievances.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You brought up something from eighteen months ago. With the exact quote. Jeong.

summer.intro: Summer Jeong, Fire ran your season and doubled your element, so your candle burns at bonfire intensity in a very small space. You're loyal, fierce and deeply private. People see someone warm and composed. Your close friends know that when you're hurt, you go silent and the room drops ten degrees. Your red flag is the cold shoulder delivered with burning eyes. You'd rather simmer than say it. In love you're all in, then all hurt, and they have to guess why. At work you'll defend your people fiercely and freeze out anyone who crossed them. The fix: words before silence. Every single time.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The silent treatment is a candle pretending to be an ice cube, Jeong.

autumn.intro: Autumn Jeong, Metal ran your birth season and your flame's job is to shape Metal. So you're a perfectionist who calls it attention to detail. People see someone thoughtful who gives the best gifts. Your friends know you've redone your grid twice this year. Your red flag is quiet control: you want things just so, and you'll adjust them yourself rather than ask. In love you might gently edit your partner: their clothes, their phrasing, their plans. At work you're the one who reformats everyone else's document. The fix: let one thing stay imperfect and see if anyone notices. Nobody will. That's the lesson.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You reformatted the shared doc at midnight. Nobody asked, Jeong. Nobody.

winter.intro: Winter Jeong, Water ran your season and Water puts out Fire, so you guard your little flame like it's the last match on earth. You're intuitive, warm in private and suspicious in public. People find you hard to read, and you like it that way. Your red flag is testing people instead of trusting them. You drop hints, see who picks them up and quietly grade the results. In love you protect yourself so carefully that partners feel like they're auditioning. At work you won't ask for help in case you look weak. The fix: tell someone what you need directly, once. No test, no hint, no secret score.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hinting, then grading who noticed, is a game nobody knows they're playing, Jeong.

strength.strong: Strong chart, Jeong. Your candle has endless fuel, which sounds lovely until it's burning a hole in someone. The blind spot: intensity. When you care, you care at full volume. When you're hurt, you're hurt for months. When you focus on someone, they feel examined. In love you can be possessive and call it devotion. With friends you expect the same level of loyalty you give, and almost nobody can match it. The fix: let people care in their own amount. Less isn't zero. Different isn't disloyal. Breathe.
strength.weak: Weak chart, Jeong, so your flame is small and you protect it fiercely, mostly by giving it away to others and keeping nothing for yourself. Classic. The blind spot: you care for everyone and then feel quietly unloved. You remember their birthdays, they forget yours, and you say nothing. In love you over-give, then go cold when it isn't returned. At work you do the thoughtful extra and nobody sees it. The fix: tell people when they've let you down, kindly and plainly. They can't fix what they don't know.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything's urgent, everything's dramatic, and your feelings arrive with sirens on. You're fun and bright, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the colour, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyse it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood. You started a new life plan on Monday. It's Wednesday. New plan.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: All that drive is wonderful. Finishing one thing will feel even better.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: three dramatic exits from group chats this year. I counted.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion lights rooms up. Count to ten before the big reply.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: same order, same route, same hoodie since 2019. I see you.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness makes people feel safe. Try one new thing for fun.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. Your honesty has made two baristas reconsider their careers.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is a gift. Wrap it in a little kindness.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've overthought this reading three times already. Stop.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is beautiful. Come back to shore when it gets heavy.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no ambition. Your five-year plan is 'see what happens'.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood just means growth needs a nudge. One small goal is plenty.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. You'd describe your best night out ever as 'fine'. Show some spark!

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can mute your joy. Do one thing just because it's fun.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth. You've changed flat, job and hair colour twice this year.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it hard to settle. A simple routine is grounding.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal. You've never said no to anyone in your life, have you?

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal means boundaries take practice. Start with one tiny no.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. Someone cried in front of you and you offered a snack.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can hide feelings. Name one out loud today.
